_meta.indication: Treatment of clinically significant hypervolemic and euvolemic hyponatremia (serum sodium < 125 mEq/L or less marked hyponatremia that is symptomatic and has resisted correction with fluid restriction), including patients with heart failure, cirrhosis, and SIADH

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; conducted exclusively in the United States
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with euvolemic or hypervolemic hyponatremia (serum sodium < 135 mEq/L) from heart failure, cirrhosis, SIADH and other causes
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: average daily AUC of change from baseline serum sodium to Day 4 and to Day 30
pivotal_trials.n: 448 patients randomized across both phase 3 studies combined (223 placebo, 225 tolvaptan); per-study N not reported in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.result: In a pooled analysis of both phase 3 studies, the average daily mean change in serum sodium through Day 4 was 4.0 mEq/L (tolvaptan) vs 0.4 mEq/L (placebo), and through Day 30 was 6.2 mEq/L vs 1.8 mEq/L; tolvaptan produced a statistically greater increase than placebo (p < 0.0001) during both periods in both studies

nct_ctgov.title: "SALT Trial" Study of Ascending Levels of Tolvaptan in Hyponatremia

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; conducted inside and outside the United States
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with euvolemic or hypervolemic hyponatremia (serum sodium < 135 mEq/L) from heart failure, cirrhosis, SIADH and other causes
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: average daily AUC of change from baseline serum sodium to Day 4 and to Day 30
pivotal_trials.n: 448 patients randomized across both phase 3 studies combined (223 placebo, 225 tolvaptan); per-study N not reported in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.result: Tolvaptan produced a statistically greater increase in serum sodium than placebo (p < 0.0001) during both periods (Day 4 and Day 30) in both studies; in the pooled analysis the average daily mean change through Day 4 was 4.0 mEq/L (tolvaptan) vs 0.4 mEq/L (placebo) and through Day 30 was 6.2 mEq/L vs 1.8 mEq/L

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Ascending Levels of Tolvaptan in Hyponatremia

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% more than placebo): thirst, dry mouth, asthenia, constipation, pollakiuria or polyuria, hyperglycemia. In the pivotal trials dry mouth occurred in 13% (tolvaptan) vs 4% (placebo) and thirst 16% vs 5%. Most serious risk is too-rapid serum sodium correction causing osmotic demyelination.
target_moa: Selective vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist; antagonizes vasopressin to increase urine water excretion (aquaresis), raising serum sodium

boxed_warning.content: Initiate and re-initiate only in a hospital where serum sodium can be monitored closely; too-rapid correction (>12 mEq/L/24 hours) can cause osmotic demyelination resulting in dysarthria, mutism, dysphagia, seizures, coma and death

rems.type: A REMS was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of overly rapid correction of serum sodium leading to osmotic demyelination; it consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments

advisory_committee.vote: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee met June 25, 2008; on whether there is adequate evidence tolvaptan can be expected to produce clinical benefits in chronic hypervolemic or euvolemic hyponatremia, the vote was 8 in favor and 3 against

summary.text: SAMSCA was a standard-review NDA (505(b)(1)) received October 23, 2007. FDA first issued a Complete Response Letter on August 22, 2008 requiring a REMS and additional safety data; after the sponsor's complete response, the application was approved May 19, 2009 with a boxed warning and a REMS consisting of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and assessment timetable. No accelerated approval, orphan, breakthrough, fast track, or priority-review designations were applied.
